requirements.text: The user never has to remember an absorbed skill name or manually pair skills; a package with procedural capabilities generates an umbrella skill exposing at most one configurable user-facing command (/<command>) and a bounded domain-rich 'Use when...' SKILL.md description for natural-language host discovery. A package containing only permanent policy emits no discoverable SKILL.md.

evidence.excerpt: The result must run identically on Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode and Hermes from the first release.
Muro is the factory: muro/, prompts/ and muro_build.py. It holds no package-specific knowledge.

requirements.text: Muro is a standard-library-only Python 3.10+ factory separate from the packages it builds (such as examples/marionette/), emitting standalone packages with shared coordination mechanics and each host's native policy channel across Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode and Hermes, with no package-specific rules leaked into muro/ or prompts/.

evidence.excerpt: sources.json defines plugin.slug, plugin.name, plugin.command, and plugin.version.
Every direct and step instruction payload includes state_dir, map_path and recorded_outputs.

requirements.text: sources.json defines the package identity (slug, name, command, version, optional description, install_policy, language, and stack rules), parameterizing dist/<slug>/, /<command>, NOTICE.md, GUIDE.html, and .<slug>/map.md while rejecting hardcoded .muro/ paths when slug != 'muro'.

evidence.excerpt: muro_build.py fails closed if plugin.slug or plugin.command is empty, non-kebab-case, or matches a reserved host command.

requirements.text: muro_build.py prevents naming collisions across three levels: stripping upstream public commands, enforcing unique capability IDs and per-source script namespaces (scripts/<source-id>/), and rejecting reserved native host commands or colliding installed plugins.

Every source declares pin, one of: release, head, static.

requirements.text: muro_build.py --check-sources verifies every source's 40-character commit SHA, declared pin mode (release tag, upstream head, or static commit), MIT or Apache-2.0 license (root or scoped license_path with nested-license checks), and UTF-8 non-binary selected_paths; --offline-pins validates manifest pins and local repositories while explicitly disclosing skipped remote fetches.

requirements.text: Capabilities carry 10 mandatory frontmatter fields (id, role, when, after, outputs, checks, intents, tools, hooks, conflicts), optional reads, needs, output_types, resumable, intent_checks and check_conditions fields, and a mandatory ## Sources section, mirrored in a 6-column ROUTER.md (id | role | when | after | outputs | intents) and strictly validated with unknown frontmatter keys rejected. A capability with more than one intent must declare intent_checks.

evidence.excerpt: Harmonizer AI synthesizes knowledge and chooses coherent responsibilities, merges, alternatives, real prerequisites and conflict resolutions.

requirements.text: Intake, harmonization and runtime task classification are performed semantically by the host LLM from source and catalog meaning; manifest order, matching labels, regex and keyword lists never decide merges, precedence or runtime routing.

evidence.excerpt: every output key has exactly one producer in a resolved plan.
Repeated capabilities in one plan use explicit step_id: <cap>#<n> with namespaced output keys.
Absent delivery preserves existing catalog bindings; declared policy and hooks belong to the release contract.
test_changed_policy_rejects_old_decision_and_evidence_without_writes

requirements.text: Python validates the host AI's explicit selections against task, stack constraints, catalog digest, conditional needs judgments, role variants, declared conflicts and single-owner outputs (supporting explicit step_id instances with namespaced outputs), failing closed without automatic substitution. When delivery.json exists its full validated declaration participates in the digest, so changed permanent policy or hook delivery invalidates previous classifications and saved-map resumes without rewriting their evidence; absent delivery preserves the previous digest format.

evidence.excerpt: Every successful build generates GUIDE.html for that release, at the package root and in each of the five independently installable host skill directories.

requirements.text: Every release generates an offline, self-contained GUIDE.html (defaulting to English, or Italian via plugin.language) at its root and in every adapter's runtime resource directory, embedding the verified Cytoscape.js bundle, declared after/needs/reads relationships and validated nonempty guide-examples.json scenarios without browser-side task classification. The guide preserves declared delivery decisions, reasons, policy text and hook wirings and uses the runtime's delivery-bound catalog digest, including for packages with no procedural capabilities.

evidence.excerpt: Maps track map_status (active or completed)... step validates outputs and batched checks in memory before publishing a single atomic state snapshot.

A step result carries its `intent`,
   its scoped `checks` and the conditions among them.

requirements.text: One-step tasks execute in direct mode whenever no active map exists, while multi-step maps support inline/stdin JSON, atomic step batches (outputs + checks), selective upstream preservation (--preserve-completed), token-bound lock recovery (unlock --token), and map completion (complete) restoring direct mode. Each step answers only the checks its capability declares for the intent chosen for that step; check results are pass, fail, not-tested or not-applicable, and not-applicable is accepted only for a check with a declared condition.

requirements.text: A package's scope is exactly what its intake absorbed, in any domain. A package may declare AI-authored discovery entries (entries.json): area skills with sharp descriptions that route into the one coordinator, hidden from the slash menu where the host allows, with every absorbed capability in an entry. An entry may declare absorbs, the names from plugin.replaces whose work it does; the build appends a sentence naming them to its description.

requirements.text: Every flow works on its second pass: preparation and eval commands are rerunnable without deleting foreign files, releases can be staged with --build --out, and a refined request amends the active map (plan --amend), carrying over only steps whose declared inputs are not redone.

evidence.excerpt: AI-authored catalog data, or an AI judgment, never a Python proxy.
**A rule names what it refers to.**

requirements.text: Facts about meaning are declared, not inferred: a capability declared resumable gets a map even as a single step; plugin.replaces lists the absorbed originals that every INSTALL.md tells the user to switch off, and the entries that absorb them name them where the host chooses a skill; a multi-intent capability declares which checks each intent answers.

evidence.excerpt: `--prepare-eval` writes the rules, compact catalog and case contexts for the host AI, never the expectations
test_eval_receives_exact_policy_and_matches_runtime_and_guide_binding

requirements.text: Routing quality is evaluated from outside: eval-cases.json holds requests with expected decisions, the host AI classifies them without seeing the expectations, and Python validates and compares. Eval preparation validates delivery.json and supplies its exact always_on policy alongside the catalog, rules and case contexts; preparation, scoring, runtime and guide share the delivery-bound digest, so old eval decisions cannot be scored as current after a policy change. Host-protocol changes are run in a real host with calls, denials, cost and sample size recorded; deterministic adapter simulations and unavailable live checks are reported separately.

evidence.excerpt: It never picks a form. An invalid document stops the build.

requirements.text: Every intake records in delivery.json what each part of a source becomes (on-demand capability, permanent session policy, active hook or dropped) with a source-grounded reason; the host AI makes that judgment with prompts/delivery.md at intake and reviews it at harmonization. Python validates shape, references, a decision for every source, the policy cap of 6000 characters for each source with an always-on decision (one shared budget, proportional to the contributing intakes) and declared active hook ownership, and never chooses a form. Loading the complete generated native plugin/package registers only its declared delivery, subject to the host's own trust, feature and permission controls; intake, build and classification never install, activate or modify host configuration. All five adapters provide a native policy channel; arbitrary source command-hook wirings are currently accepted only for Claude Code and Codex, with unsupported wirings rejected and host requirements stated in INSTALL.md. Packages without delivery.json retain no automatic policy or hook registration.

evidence.excerpt: An explicit, valid permanent policy is a useful package without procedural skills.
test_policy_only_release_has_no_fabricated_capability
test_policy_only_runtime_requires_ai_and_accepts_no_match_without_state

requirements.text: A valid explicit always-on delivery may form a package with zero procedural capabilities: capabilities/ may be absent or empty, ROUTER.md retains its valid six-column header with no capability rows, and guide-examples.json remains nonempty with authored no_match or needs_clarification decisions. Build preserves runtime resources, provenance, notices and GUIDE.html in every adapter but emits no fabricated capability, discovery entry or SKILL.md. If its runtime is called, plan still requires an explicit AI classification and never invents a coordinator fallback. Empty packages without a valid nonempty declared policy, including dropped-only delivery, remain invalid.

evidence.excerpt: Emit Claude Code's native additive system-prompt module.
Codex's native developer-instruction channel, plus explicitly declared source hooks.
Expose the skills and, when declared, one structured Pi system-prompt section.
A dependency-free OpenCode V2 plugin: skills and optional outgoing system text.
Emit a native Hermes plugin; the host owns prompt assembly and permissions.

requirements.text: Declared policy is delivered through additive host-native channels without replacing existing core instructions: Claude Code uses a prompt.compose module adding a named system-prompt section; Codex uses SessionStart and SubagentStart hooks adding developer instructions, with startup, resume, clear, compact and fork session matching; Pi uses before_agent_start with systemPromptOptions.sections; OpenCode V2 uses context, compaction, generate and title session hooks that append a policy text part only when absent; Hermes uses register_system_prompt_section after memory. The full native adapter, not merely its skill files, must be loaded. INSTALL.md declares the required APIs and host controls; Hermes reports an explicit warning when its prompt-section API is unavailable instead of claiming policy activation. Claude Code, Pi and OpenCode composition preserves other host sections and does not accumulate duplicate policy sections.

evidence.excerpt: Keep declared argv and installed paths out of the host's shell syntax.
test_host_shell_preserves_argv_stdin_and_exit_without_expanding_data
Explicit JSON keeps policy starting with { or [ from becoming hook controls.

requirements.text: Generated command-hook dispatch preserves literal declared argv, installed paths, stdin, stdout, stderr and process exit status across supported host shells. A standard-library Python trampoline decodes command data, resolves the host's plugin-root variable and <package_root> after shell dispatch, then runs the declared argv with shell=False; shell metacharacters in arguments or installed paths are not reinterpreted by the host shell. Codex session-context --hook-event emits the policy as hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext with the matching hookEventName, so policy text beginning with JSON syntax cannot become hook-control fields. Unreadable or invalid declared session policy returns a visible failure; absent delivery emits no policy.

evidence.excerpt: A release carries an original

requirements.text: A release carries an original source file only when a capability reads it at run time. A source may declare intake_only_paths: selected files the intake AI read and restated or dropped; they remain in the intake workbench, are absent from scripts/<source-id>/ in the release and in every adapter, each pattern must match a selected file, and a capability body that names the packaged path of such a file is rejected. The AI decides per file; Python removes and checks.

evidence.excerpt: installed with exactly the commands written there

requirements.text: Each generated adapter can be installed with its host's own command: the Claude Code and Codex adapter folders carry a single-plugin marketplace manifest (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json, .agents/plugins/marketplace.json) whose plugin source is the folder itself, and INSTALL.md of Claude Code, Codex, Pi and OpenCode ends with an Install section giving the command and what is active after it. A command appears there only after it ran on the real host. The Codex section states that declared hooks, and the policy they deliver, are not active until the user trusts them in /hooks.

evidence.excerpt: The substance is the source's

requirements.text: What a source prescribes (its rules, numbers, conditions, exceptions and limits) is not altered in whatever form the AI chose for it (capability, permanent policy, hook). The text that selects and starts a part (a hook's text, a capability body as its entry prompt, intent and entry descriptions) is written or regenerated by the host LLM for the package and never drops, weakens, strengthens or invents a rule. An activated capability refers to the packaged original, kept whole and untouched, for the parts the task needs, by file and section; a selected file the generated plugin does not need is removed as a file and as a reference. What a source prescribes changes only to guarantee harmonization and coexistence under the package's principles, never for size, style or taste; each change is the smallest that removes the collision and is recorded with that collision in delivery.json or in the capability's Sources. Permanent policy keeps the source's own words, and every line in it that is not a source's is marked with the package name.

def test_a_check_of_another_intent_is_rejected_and_nothing_is_recorded

requirements.text: Evidence describes the step it is bound to. A capability with more than one intent declares intent_checks, every intent mapped to the checks a step serving it answers, with every check in at least one intent; check_conditions gives a check that applies only in some tasks its case in plain language. Both are AI judgments made at harmonization; Python checks their shape. The runtime returns each step's intent, scoped checks and conditions, rejects a check outside the step's scope or a not-applicable without a condition without recording anything, refuses a state holding either, and completes a map on exactly the scoped checks. A step reached only through after has no chosen intent, so its capability's intents share one scope. A catalog that declares a scope or condition binds it in the catalog digest; one without keeps its digest.

The generated entry description is

def test_the_built_skills_name_the_originals_and_keep_the_umbrella_text_whole

requirements.text: A package names the originals it absorbs where the host chooses a skill. An entry declares absorbs, names from plugin.replaces judged by the harmonizing AI from the capabilities' sources; the build appends after the unchanged AI-authored description a sentence naming them and telling the host to use the entry instead, also when the user names one, within the 1024-character limit. The umbrella says that its entries name what it absorbs, or lists plugin.replaces when there are no entries, and its fixed text is short enough not to cut the AI-authored description. Python checks the names and lengths and never decides which entry absorbs what.
